examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Area of a Triangle by Solving for a Variable Given an Angle
examples.problem:
In square units rounded to one decimal place, find the area of $\triangle ABC$ shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946119/assets/6049cd70d2bd6b269cead37481bcebc8403f35d90d4fc2cbb07d162243015d00.png)
examples.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
\mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $m\angle{B} = 23^\circ.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{B},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({23}^{∘}) & =\frac{x-1}{2x} \\ 2x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({23}^{∘}) & =x-1 \\ 1 & =x-2x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({23}^{∘}) \\ 1 & =x(1-2\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({23}^{∘})) \\ x & =\frac{1}{1-2\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({23}^{∘})} \\ x & =6.620\,3…\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =2x=2(6.620\,3…)=13.240\,6…, \\ AC & =x-1=(6.620\,3…)-1=5.620\,3….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}(5.620\,3…)(13.240\,6…) \\  & =37.208\,0… \\  & ≈37.2,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the one decimal place.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946119/assets/434c2ac4c8b4043ad191bf23eff129ba79b26b0b7b838df4658df639ba140504.png)

Given that $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2},$ where $\theta =m∠A.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overset{―}{BC}$ opposite to $∠A.$ Hence, we can use the sine ratio to find the length of the hypotenuse $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \frac{1}{2} & =\frac{8}{AB} \\ AB & =8(2) \\ AB & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the Pythagorean Theorem to find the missing side $AC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =\sqrt{A{B}^{2}-B{C}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{16}^{2}-{8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{256-64} \\  & =\sqrt{192} \\  & =8\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 8\cdot (8\sqrt{3}) \\  & =32\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
